utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody, and good morning, Madam Registrar. Could you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, ma'am. All the accused are here. From the Defence teams, I only notice the absence of Mr. Ostojic. Prosecution is Mr. McCloskey, Mr. Nicholls, and Mr. Vanderpuye. Any preliminaries? We have incidentally in relation to the videolink, we have received the response from the Nikolic Defence teams. I understand that the Popovic one -- yes -- is being made available this morning. We haven't read it of course. We'll go through it and come back to you after the first break or during the second break. Any preliminaries?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is about what was mentioned yesterday, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes. I've spoken with my friends, Mr. Zivanovic, yesterday and this morning. I think we have an agreement both sides are going to proceed, we are all going to proceed in good faith and he will withdraw his motion. I'm going to send him an e-mail before the first break and he's going to read that, and then I think we will have this issue resolved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Mr. Nicholls and I thank you as well, Mr. Zivanovic. I think we can bring in the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Momcilovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I also wish to welcome you to this Tribunal on behalf of the Trial Chamber. You're about to start giving evidence very soon. Madam Usher, will hand you a piece of paper with the text of a solemn declaration that you are required to make before you start giving evidence, and that is equivalent to an oath in some jurisdictions and it is an undertaking that you will be testifying the truth. Please read it out aloud and that will be your solemn undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, sir. Please take a seat and make yourself comfortable. You have met Mr. Vanderpuye already. He will be the first one to go. He will ask you some questions for the Prosecution -- on behalf of the Prosecution. He will then be followed by members of the Defence teams on cross-examination. If you keep your answers as precise and as concise as possible, I hope that we'll be able to send you home very quickly. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning to you, Your Honours. Good morning, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Momcilovic. Before we get started --

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning to you too.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Before we get started, I just wanted to remind you of a couple of things. The first would be to try to keep your voice up so that the interpreters can hear you, and we can all follow what you're saying. The second is to allow a short pause between question and answer so there is time to translate or interpret what you said, and also, if there is anything that I've asked you that's unclear to you, please feel free to ask me to rephrase the question and I'll do my best to state it in a way that is better understood by you. As a --

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Would you please state your full name for the record?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Bozo Momcilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Momcilovic, where were you born?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: On the 25th of January 1962 in Opravdici Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And where do you currently reside?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: In Kravica village in Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you briefly tell us what your educational background is?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I graduated from the school of economics in 1986 in Belgrade, and I'm currently the head of finances and accountancy in the forestry service.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: How long have you been employed by the forestry service?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Since 1987.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in 1987, can you tell us whom you were employed by?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I started working in the brick works in Bratunac and I stayed there until 1998, when I joined the forestry management services of Srebrenica and, again, I repeat, I've been employed as the head of finances. Between 1992 and 1994 I was the general manager of the state-owned brick works in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Have you received any military training?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Save for the compulsory military service in 1980, 1981, in the former JNA, I did not receive any other military training. I served in Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, have you performed any work obligation?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Between 1992 and September 1994, I had work obligation as the general manager or the acting director of the brick works. Then I was mobilised and I joined the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And when was your mobilisation to the army?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Around the end of September or the beginning of October 1994, I joined the 1st Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade and at the beginning of December I was transferred to the command of the Bratunac Brigade as the logistics man.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When you were first transferred to the Bratunac Brigade, to which battalion were you transferred or to what unit in particular were you transferred?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I served in the 1st Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade, it was mostly composed of the locals of Kravica village, and I was the assistant commander for logistics.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And to whom did you report in this capacity?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I spent the very little time, maybe about a month or a month and a half, and I worked with Lazo Ostojic, who was the battalion commander, he was the first Lieutenant at the time. He was very young. He had just graduated from the military academy, and as I've just said, I did not spend much time there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what were your duties and responsibilities, if you could just briefly tell us?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Logistics, food, clothes, footwear, those would be the basic duties I had with regard to the battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what was your rank at the time?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: The one that I got from the former army, as a Sergeant but I never actually received any other ranks.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, you said that you spent only a brief time in the 1st Battalion. You were then transferred to the command of the brigade. And in what capacity did you serve out that tenure?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to a decision of the brigade commander, Colonel Ognjenovic, I was transferred to the logistics command to work under Major Trisic to serve as the logistics man in the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you recall what your specific title was?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Logistics means that it had to do with food, clothing and footwear of the members of the Bratunac Brigade. We had a number of storages or depots where this was all stored, and it was our duty to distribute all those necessities to the troops who were in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Well, maybe I've miscommunicated the question. I was just asking you if you remember what your specific title was as opposed to what your duties were. If you don't, that's fine too.

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I was the desk officer of the logistics with the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And with respect to the duties that you had at that time, did you have occasion to deal with the municipal authorities in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was a common practice for the industry of Bratunac to provide some of the supplies for the brigade. Maticic [phoen] would attend the meetings of the municipality, sometimes it would even be the brigade commander, and they would talk about the requirements of some things such as cigarettes and other stuff, especially for the reception of soldiers. I was the one who would later on collect stuff from the companies who had made a commitment to our commander to provide certain things such as fuel or cigarettes or such like.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And how long did you remain in this particular position?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I remained there up to February 1996. I was demobilised and I returned to the brick works, to my former position as the head of finances.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I just want to direct your attention to the beginning of July 1995, if I may, and ask you a few questions about that. Do you recall in the beginning of July 1995 where you were assigned?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: At the beginning of July 1995, pursuant to a decision of the assistant commander for logistics of the Drina Corps, Colonel Acamovic, I received an order to be transferred to the forward command post at Pribicevac to coordinate the logistics there. Since I had been the desk officer of the logistics at the Bratunac Brigade, they had estimated that it would be a logical thing for the logistics man from the Bratunac Brigade to go to the forward command post. On the 4th I received this order and on the 5th I already arrived in Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you recall what the order directed that you do there, your duties or responsibilities?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Receipt of foodstuffs and distribution at the Pribicevac locality for the troops who would be deployed in that area. In that area there were troops not only from the Bratunac Brigade but also from the Zvornik Brigade, from the Sekovici Brigade, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. We will get to that in just a minute. But the order that you received, was it an oral order, was it a written order?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: It was a written order, and later on, it was forwarded electronically to the Bratunac Brigade. I personally took the order on the 4th in the corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And was the order directed to you or was it directed to your superior, Major Trisic?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: It was directed to the Bratunac Brigade, with an indication that I should be transferred to the Pribicevac region. When I showed this to Major Trisic, I realised that he had been already aware of that decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And -- all right. Now, you mentioned in your previous answer that there were troops from Bratunac, from the Bratunac Brigade, Zvornik Brigade, Sekovici Brigade and so on and so forth. And I just wanted to get to the so on and so forth. Can you tell us what other units were stationed or were in that vicinity at the time that you were there?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there were the troops of the 3rd Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade and also the workers battalion, meaning people who had work obligation during that time but they spent two or three days in Pribicevac, and then they were deployed in the Milici sector at which point I lost all contact with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, the troops that were deployed there, were they deployed there in relation to the operations concerning Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Save for the 3rd Battalion, that was there all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And while you were there, from whom did you receive your orders?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I received my specific orders through the liaison officer, Mr. Jevdjevic and General Krstic. They communicated to me the requirements in terms of food, cigarettes, and other stuff.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And were these orders communicated to you from General Krstic directly or through the normal chain of command?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: The normal chain of command, through the liaison officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in terms of -- through the liaison officer meaning Mr. Jevdjevic, is that your understanding?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Jevdjevic, yes, yes, Jevdjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, did you have a commander of logistics at the IKM, the forward command post of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: The commander for logistics of the Drina Corps or the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Who was your specific commander while you were at the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: At the IKM, there were no other officers for -- save for Krstic and the liaison officer, Jevdjevic. I did not see anybody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Did you receive any orders from Major Trisic during this period of time?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: No. They just provided support in terms of receiving food on the ground. I did not receive any distribution orders from Major Trisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you report to him at all?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I did not send any written reports. There was just one oral exchange during the course of his visit to the Pribicevac sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you have any direct dealings with Colonel Acamovic?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Sorry, that didn't receive a translation.

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: No. Did not have any contacts with him. I did not receive any orders from him either.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you report to him?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I just want to get into, if I could, another area which is just the general for you to describe generally the area where the IKM was located, and if you could, could you just tell us, to the best that you can, how it was laid out, the number of buildings or the types of buildings that were there?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: It was a Serb village that was torched in 1992. All the houses were destroyed. The 3rd Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade arrived on the lines in 1993, sometime in March, and they managed to adapt those buildings to suit their needs, to protect them, and to locate their command there, together with the logistics of the battalion. Those were the only facilities made of so to say hard material. The logistics command had their vehicles, and they put up tents during the operation that took place in 1995. The diameter or the perimeter of all these facilities was about 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in terms of facilities, where did people sleep, where did people eat, and from where was business normally conducted, that is operations and things of that nature?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Save for the command of the 3rd Battalion and the logistics personnel that were billeted in these facilities, the troops were deployed along the lines where they had their trenches and that's where they were billeted.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in terms of the commanding officers, where exactly were they housed and/or worked?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the 3rd Battalion had his office in Pribicevac. It was a little room where he kept his papers. The liaison officer slept with the troops in the tents. General Krstic never spent a night there. He would arrive in the morning and leave in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Was it the case that other officers also left at the end of the day and came in the morning?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Those who visited General Krstic left. Nobody stayed. Only Colonel Vukota, who stayed with the 3rd Battalion for a longer period of time and who had been with the battalion before July 1995 spent more time there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, during the period of time that you were there, and just so that the record is clear, let me ask you first when it is that you left there and when it is that you got there so that we can establish that for the record.

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I arrived there on the 5th of July 1995, and I stayed until 11th 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. So during the period of time that you were there, was it the case that there were people that visited the forward command post, that were there to survey the general area of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is it possible to see Srebrenica or the -- or survey the operation concerning Srebrenica from that location in Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: You can see just one part of Srebrenica from that place, and the operation could be surveyed because the location is high up. It is an elevation point.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. If I could have in e-court please P02870. All right. If we could just maybe blow this up a little bit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which? Can you indicate exactly the part you would like our staff to blow up for you, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Just so that Srebrenica and, if you can see Pribicevac on the right-hand side of the screen, are basically the top and the bottom of the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could make it that big. If we could make it just a little bit bigger, I think? Okay. Great.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you see that map before you, Mr. Momcilovic?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I would like to do is have the witness mark the map, if that's possible.

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Pribicevac. What am I supposed to mark?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I would just like you, if you can see it on the map, to indicate where it is in the vicinity of Pribicevac you can see the operation or Srebrenica, if you can indicate that on the map.

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: From the Pribicevac sector, from the elevation 01013, from Divljakinje elevation 789, you can see Srebrenica because Srebrenica is in a valley, and the valley is meandering, so there is no elevation from which you can see the whole valley. The elevation points that I've mentioned provide you a good view of certain parts of Srebrenica. There was this Tucak hill close to Srebrenica and Biljeg, which is another elevation point from which you can see different parts of Srebrenica. All that is roughly along this red line.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Let me just, if we could zoom out just a minute or if we can zoom out a little bit, I'll have him mark those particular areas. If we could go down just a little so that Srebrenica is at the top of the-- all right. Now, Mr. Momcilovic, I'd ask for you to mark with an X, and if you could, a small arrow, pointing in the direction from which you can -- the direction you can see for each of the locations that you've mentioned.

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: From Bukova Glava and Tucak along the Cicevac [phoen] creek, you can see one part of the Srebrenica canyon. From Pribicevac you can also see the first part of Srebrenica from the entrance into the town and from Kvarac, up there, and from Divljakinje you can see another part of Srebrenica closer to the exit from Srebrenica. I know the area very well because this is where -- the route I would take to get to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I would like you to do is actually write on the screen with the pen you have in your hand, you can write on the screen, put an X at the location and then a small arrow pointing the direction that can be seen for each of the ones that you've mentioned.

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]. Roughly here. And you can't see any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Are you familiar with an elevation by the name of Javor?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but it is a bit further down from Bukova Glava and Tucak. You can see the area in the vicinity of Srebrenica, but you can't see the town itself because the view is prevented by Tucak. It is right before Zeleni Jadar, in the direction of Skelani.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If I could, I'd like you to initial this drawing on the bottom left hand corner and put today's date, please.

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]. The 22nd?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes. All right. Thank you, Mr. Momcilovic. I'd just like to have this up on the screen for a little while longer. Could you tell us approximately, with respect to the X that you placed next to March on the top right-hand side of the screen, and the X that you placed next to Tucak on the bottom right-hand side of the screen, approximately how far those are respectively from Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: The elevation point 1013 is maybe three to three and a half kilometres away from it, not more. As Tucak hill, the elevation near Bukova Glava, could be about five or six kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Momcilovic. I'd like to take you to a different area. Now, you've indicated before that while you were stationed at the IKM, there were a number of units that were also present there or stationed there. Were there any other units that arrived there or came through there while you were assigned to that location?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: The workers battalion arrived there and went through there. They only stayed one day, I believe they left on the other day, and I don't really know about other units. I haven't seen any apart from the units of the Zvornik Brigade, but they had been there when I arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: While you were there, did you see any high-ranking officers?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, some would come.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, did you see, for example, General Mladic, while you were there?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And on how many occasions did you see General Mladic while you were there?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: A few times.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you see General Zivanovic there?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He only came once.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And did you see General Gvero there?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He only came once.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you recall the specific circumstances under which he came?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, were you familiar with General Gvero in 1995, July?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I knew that he was the general in charge of morale in the army of Republika Srpska, but I had never encountered him before.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Had you ever seen him before?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Possibly on TV or in the newspapers but not in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what were the circumstances under which you saw him while you were stationed at the IKM?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: It was on the 9th of July, around noon. He arrived with my commander, Major Trisic, and Mr. Davidovic, the president of the Executive Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And how is it that you remember that that occurred on the 9th of July?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Around about that day, the stage of the separation of the enclaves of Zepa and Srebrenica was completed, and it was an event to remember. That's why I still know that. It was a day or two before the end of my job.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what was it that you were doing at the time that they arrived?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: At the moment when they arrive, I was doing my regular routines, and the purpose of the visit of Major Trisic was to examine the situation with regard to logistics, and the storage facilities were placed in front of the general's quarters so it happened that I met Major Trisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did Major Trisic come there to see you specifically or was your meeting a happenstance?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: It was a happenstance. I wasn't even aware that he was coming to visit.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And had he visited you while you were at the forward command post at any time prior to that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: You mean Major Trisic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: No. That was only three or four days so that I had enough supplies.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, at the time that General Gvero arrived with Mr. Davidovic and Major Trisic, was there anybody else present, either with them or with you?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: There was no one with them, and the guys from the 3rd Battalion were with me. The assistant commander of the 3rd Battalion, Dragoljub Ristic and his assistant Misa Davidovic, who was Davidovic's son.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you have a conversation with Major Trisic at that time?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: It was a very brief, purely informative conversation, about what the situation was like, what we had, what we were lacking, no special conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you have any conversation with either General Gvero or with Mr. Davidovic at that time?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe a spontaneous exchange but nothing special. How are you doing? How is life? Along those lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And approximately how long were you in their presence?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Five minutes, maybe, not more.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And following that period of time, where did -- what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: The three of them went to see General Krstic, who was some 30 metres away. They saluted the general there and they sat down.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And was General Krstic -- you say General Krstic was in his quarters; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they weren't really quarters. It was an improvised facilities, some tables, chairs, in fact it was a tent.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And was there anybody else there at that time?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: The liaison officer, Jevdjevic and Colonel Vukota who were in the immediate vicinity of General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the name of the Colonel again?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel Vukota, I'm not sure of his exact name. I know him as Colonel Vukota. Perhaps his real name was Vukovic, but we called him Vukota and everybody knew him by that name or nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And were you able to observe what transpired when General Gvero, Major Trisic went to the tent, what happened after they arrived there?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: We saw them salute each other and sit down, and there were some rookie soldiers there and they had a drink, et cetera, but we were in no position to hear what they were talking about. We were too far away.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And about how long were they together?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, my estimate is that it may have been about an hour, possibly a few minutes longer, but not longer than an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you have an opportunity to see when the meeting broke up or when they separated?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: When the meeting was over, they passed us by again. They had to pass us by. And then they left.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When they left did they leave together, or did they leave separately?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: No. They left together, as they had come together.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And just so that we're clear on the record, since I haven't asked you, who exactly left, and --

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: General Gvero, Major Trisic, and Mr. Davidovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And when they left, did they leave in a vehicle, did they leave on foot?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: They had come in a vehicle that didn't enter our position, so I didn't know where -- whether that same vehicle was waiting for them again outside. I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So you didn't have an opportunity to actually see them leave the area where you were?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I did see when they left, but I don't know by which means of transportation they left.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know which direction they went in?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: They went toward Bratunac because there is no other direction to take from up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You mentioned that you saw General Gvero in the IKM while you were there only one time.

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not he was there only on that one occasion?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know that was the only time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, at the time that he was there, that you saw him there, was General Mladic there?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: No, he wasn't, only General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: During your term there -- well, let me ask a different question. Are you familiar with an individual by the name of Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know him personally but I have heard of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what about a Colonel Beara?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: The same applies to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And were you familiar with them in early July 1995?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Have you seen either of them before early July 1995?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you see them at the forward command post while you were there?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, once, with the late Miroslav Deronjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what were the circumstances under which you saw them?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I think that they came by to see the view from Pribicevac. Apart from that I don't know the purpose of their visit.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Did they meet with anybody while they were there?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I was in no position to see that because I had my own work to do, so I didn't welcome them or greet them or anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Did you have any contact with Mr. Deronjic while he was there with them?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, if you hadn't seen either before, how did you know it was them that you saw then?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I had heard from people who knew them, because I personally didn't know either of them. They said, the people -- the others were talking about two guys arriving with Deronjic and Popovic. I knew Deronjic because he was a teacher when I -- when I was a student.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The guys who mentioned whom these two men were, did they tell you anything about them?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: People were saying that they were security officers. I don't know about these things, and so even today I don't know what security officers do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, did you have an opportunity to see them at any other time, either in person or in the media or in some other way?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: No. I have never seen them since, except perhaps on TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in terms of who you saw on TV, does that correspond with what your recollection or memory was of the people that you saw in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me but he didn't say that he saw them. He said that he perhaps saw them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Except when he says "except perhaps on TV," this is what he actually said. Did you see them on TV or didn't you see them on TV?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw them at Pribicevac, and I also saw them on TV later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So at that point, I think we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because my -- anyway, let's leave it because to me, "except perhaps on TV," basically meant that he saw them on TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I understand my friend's objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Even though strictly speaking the English way of putting it would allow for some doubt, but he's eliminated that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. My question to you was whether or not who you saw on TV corresponded with your memory or your recollection of who you saw then in July?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let him be specific. Let's go one by one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's start with General Gvero, please. Did you see General Gvero on TV?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So then please proceed with your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: My question actually related to Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic. With respect to Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic, did you see him on TV?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Most probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And with respect to Colonel Beara, did you see him on TV?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And after having seen them on TV, do you have any doubt as to whom you saw in July 1995, that is whether it was Colonel Beara and Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you have occasion -- well, let me rephrase -- let me ask a different question. Do you recall when it was that you saw?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: According to my memory, it may have been on the day of the bombing of the NATO forces in the area around Pribicevac. So around -- around the 11th of July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is there any special reason why it is you remember having seen them?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: There is no special reason, but I think that it was -- that is when it was because on that day, my job at IKM was finished, and nobody else came later on. We moved to Bratunac and arrived there in the evening hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: After your job was finished and you returned to Bratunac, did you return to the brigade command where you'd been originally stationed?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I returned and reported to Major Trisic, and I went to see my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And when was it that you actually returned to duty at the brigade command?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: On the 15th or 16th. I'm not sure. It probably it was the 16th. I was away for three or four days, and I continued to work in the area of logistics. I had no special assignments.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could just go into private session for a moment, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly, let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Just bear with me for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Momcilovic, thank you very much. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can I have a revised estimate from everybody? Mr. Zivanovic, you have indicated or you had requested 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Now we'll reduce it. 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ostojic for Mr. Beara -- for the record now, I didn't want to interrupt the testimony of the witness, but Mr. Ostojic entered the courtroom soon after the testimony of the witness started. Yes, Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, I apologise for coming late. We still have about 45 minutes, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Nikolic? You had requested ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, ten to 15 minutes at the most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We announced ten minutes, Your Honours, and we'll adhere to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Ms. Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have modified our request and after having heard the witness, we have decided not to cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam. Mr. Krgovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Half an hour, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And Mr. Haynes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Nothing, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That basically should leave us time also to start with the next witness. Where is Mr. McCloskey? I can't see him behind there. That should leave us time to start with the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. That witness should be available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. I just wanted to alert you to that. All right. Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Momcilovic.

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The Defence of the general would like to ask some questions about your testimony today. Since the two of us speak the same language, I would like to ask you to wait for the interpretation before you answer so that there is no overlapping for the sake of the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In your testimony today, you said from the 5th until the 11th of July, you were at the forward command post of Pribicevac, is that so?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: These units that you mentioned in the examination-in-chief, the workers brigade, the part of the Zvornik Brigade and others, they are all parts of the Drina Corps, is that so?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: As far as you know, only these units took part in the Srebrenica operation?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, at least in the area where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The operations of the Drina Corps were commanded by General Krstic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you were at a place from which you were able to see how he was commanding and leading the operation?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was in the immediate vicinity so I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Nobody else assisted General Krstic apart from the officers you saw during the conduct of the operation?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from the liaison officer, Jevdjevic, and Colonel Vukota, I saw nobody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Nobody came from outside to take over command, to give orders to the units, and to interfere with the commanding duties of General Krstic, as far as you were able to see, is that so?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were some informative visits only.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: From the position where you were, you were able to follow the conduct of the Srebrenica operation, is that so?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was able to see well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: During that period of your stay at the forward command post, the town of Srebrenica, was it shelled by the artillery?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: No. There was no shelling, no artillery shelling, because I work in that town now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know about an order about the manner of conducting the operation against Srebrenica by General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was a ban on shelling in order to spare the civilians. We are talking about an area that was three or four kilometres deep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you something about the stay of General Gvero at the IKM in Pribicevac. When general Gvero came, did you hear him say where from he had arrived?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know where he came from, when he came from Mr. Davidovic and Major Trisic. We received some printed matter at the time, some newspapers at the time. You could not buy any magazines or newspapers in Bratunac at the time. All of those were Belgrade editions, so I suppose that he had come from there. I did not hear the conversation, but it was only logical that the general would bring all that printed matter because he was in charge of the morale of the troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Something has not been translated and not recorded in the transcript. You received it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we received the printed matter when the three of them came, Davidovic and Trisic did not have any where to buy newspapers and magazines in Bratunac. I suppose that it was general Gvero who had obtained these magazines and brought them to the IKM.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have the feeling that we are going too fast. Gauging from the speed the interpreters are translating, we are going too fast. Mr. Momcilovic, if you could, please, and you too, Mr. Krgovic, allow a short pause between question and answer. The reason is that we don't understand your language, and you both speak the same language. So the interpreters who are translating to us in English and French have to catch up with what you are saying and translate, and while they are translating, you continue talking. So that makes it difficult for them. Yes, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you have heard the words of the Honourable Judge. Let's both of us make sure to observe those words. What printed matter are we talking about? What newspapers was it? Dailies, the usual dailies or something else?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: The dailies, daily newspapers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Momcilovic, you have just described for us when the Prosecutor showed you the elevations from which you could observe Srebrenica, General Gvero did not go to those elevation points to observe Srebrenica, to see the town, on the occasion when he visited the IKM; is that correct? He just sat down on the benches together with General Krstic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Just one more thing. What is the procedure, what was the procedure, rather, when high-ranking officer came at the IKM? Was he supposed to report to somebody, to inform them that he had arrived and where he was? Do you know what I'm saying?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, and judging from the common practice of the Bratunac Brigade, including the Pribicevac IKM, almost all officers who arrived at the Pribicevac sector or the command would normally report to the base, to somebody there. The liaison officer was at their disposal, and I suppose that almost everybody, not"almost," but everybody reported to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was officer Jevdzevic present at the time?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see Gvero addressing Jevdzevic at the time?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Jevdzevic was present during that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please repeat slowly the name of this officer?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Jevdzevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please spell?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: J-E-V-D-Z-E-V-I-C.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: At the time when General Gvero stayed at Pribicevac, in that area, there was no fighting; would I be correct in saying this?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: The separation of Zepa and Srebrenica enclaves had already been completed and there was no operation going on during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: From the place where you were, did you see General Gvero and Krstic moving away from Trisic, or were they together all the time?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: They were together all the time, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Just for the transcript, here in the transcript, it says that "he moved away from Trisic." Just to be clear, you have just told us that not for a single moment did General Gvero and General Gvero separate from the others?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. From Davidovic, Trisic, Jukota [phoen], Jevdzevic, they were together all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Again, the transcript is incorrect. General Gvero and General Krstic did not separate from the others, is that what you've just told us?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did not separate from the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe this is a convenient moment for a break. I will have no further questions unless, after consultations with my client, I am instructed otherwise. In that case, I might have some questions after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So we can have the break now. In the meantime, Mr. Krgovic is to be allowed -- I'm addressing the security, is to be allowed a short time, an opportunity, to consult with his client before they are -- so we'll have a 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So Mr. Krgovic, you had to update us, whether you wish to put further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Momcilovic. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who wishes to go second? Yes, Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I would like to, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you introduce yourself to -- with the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Momcilovic my name is John Ostojic and I represent Mr. Ljubisa Beara. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you some questions here to clarify some of your testimony, sir, and to you as I did to the Court, I apologise for coming late this morning. But I read what you said earlier, so I think we can proceed. But I apologise for coming late before you started to testify. Sir, let me ask you this: When did -- your commander in the Drina Corps, who was it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: In the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: The commander of my Bratunac Brigade was General Blagojevic and the corps commander was General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, when did you move from the Bratunac Brigade to the Drina Corps? What was the exact date, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: The Bratunac Brigade was part of the Drina Corps, and pursuant to Colonel Acamovic's order, the assistant commander of General Krstic for logistics, I was transferred on the 4th of July and already on the 5th I was in the Pribicevac sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The commander according to your recollection of the Drina Corps on or about the 5th of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was a shake-up involving General Krstic and General Zivanovic. I don't know when. When I arrived at the IKM, General Krstic was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So according to you, sir, when you came to the IKM, on the 5th of July 1995, General Krstic was already appointed as the commander of the Drina Corps, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether he had been appointed. He was at the Pribicevac IKM.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And sir, you were at the IKM for, as you say, approximately six days from July 5th through July 11th, 1995, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And is it your testimony that when you left the IKM on July 11th, 1995, that you left because the Srebrenica and Zepa separation of the enclave was already complete? Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: The separation was completed, and the Serb forces had entered Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But when did they take over Srebrenica? Do you remember the date?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: On the 11th in the evening or late in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And who ordered you to leave the IKM on the 11th?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: When General Krstic left the IKM, we received an order from the liaison officer to pack everything and to return everything to the logistics base in Bratunac because everybody was moving from the IKM in Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So the day Srebrenica falls, is it your testimony then that evening you went basically on a four or five day vacation or leave? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I did not say that. I visited my family in Osamsko. I went to see my in laws because they had fled Kravica. I stayed there for four or five days. There were no particular assignments. During that period of time, so I spent those four or five days with my family, with my in laws, my wife, and my children.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So you're one of the persons who is in charge or had some responsibility for logistics of the rear services of Drina Corps, and the Serbs just take over Srebrenica, if you will, Zepa doesn't happen yet, correct, until after Srebrenica, is that true?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So at that point you leave from the 11th to the 15th? You're not around to assist your fellow soldiers or your fellow men while they're taking over Srebrenica? Do you know what happened after the 11th through the 15th of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I was the quartermaster of the Bratunac Brigade. I was in charge of the cigarettes, food, the clothes, and footwear. During that period of time, I had Officer Cvijetinovic who was in charge of all the current affairs in the Bratunac Brigade, and all the other units were supplied in their own way. All this allowed me to be absent for four or five days from that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, do you know what happened from July 11th through July 15th, 1995, while you were gone?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't around during those four or five days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, couldn't you be more specific as to location at least?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I am. I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I was getting to that. Sir, so I know your testimony is you were in the IKM. Afterwards, where did you come, when you came back on the 15th, where did you go to, what place?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: To the rear of the Bratunac Brigade. I went back to my workplace, to my storages, and I went back to my regular duties. When this was done, that meant that the order for me to stay at the IKM expired and I returned back under the command of Major Trisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And you came back to Bratunac, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now I just want to ask you, do you know anything that may have occurred from July 11th through July 15th, 1995 in Potocari? Have you ever heard of that village or town?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I know the town but I didn't go up there, and I really don't know. I only know the hearsay, but I never went there myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How about anything that may have happened in Bratunac after July 15th, 1995? Did you learn about any Muslim prisoners being detained or held in Bratunac in 1995, July 15th, for example?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I was in my storages and my depots. I did not leave them. I didn't go anywhere. I don't know whether anything happened or what happened. I know that the civilian population was being transferred in the direction of Tuzla, but I really don't know what, when, how.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned a gentleman by the name of Srbislav Davidovic. Can you tell me what your relationship, if any, is with him? Are you friends, are you neighbours, both?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: We are not neighbours. I know the man.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. I think that part was heard in private session. Judge Kwon is drawing my attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's a general question and I recognise -- I don't want to elaborate in public, open session, but I can in private, if the Court wishes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I think it's in an abundance of caution we should proceed in private session, but I think the general nature of the question at this point is okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have any further questions? I mean I have to ask you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, and I do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then why don't we go straight into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough, if the Court allows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, we are back in public session. And you testified in the Momir Nikolic sentencing hearing, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I was a defence witness. I was a character witness. They asked me whether I knew him before 1992, after 1996. It was in open session. Momir Nikolic resided very close to my wife. I know him from when we were children. He wanted me to testify on his behalf and I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: He was actually a neighbour of yours, your house was right -- his house was right next door to your parents' house, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: No. Not my parents. Momir Nikolic, we are talking about? His house was about eight or nine kilometres away from mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And have you testified or offered to be a Defence witness for any other accused other than Momir Nikolic for his character?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, for who?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel Blagojevic. I was a quartermaster in his brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We know that. But I didn't really get a full appreciation. You were also going to testify, and you gave a written statement for the Defence of Colonel Blagojevic as well, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And that statement was confirmed by the representatives of the Tribunal in Bratunac. They acknowledged that what I stated at the time, I was willing to repeat in court, and they took my statement as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I read your statement and let me understand it because I know you were gone from the 11th through the 15th and don't know what happened in Potocari, Bratunac, or anywhere in that area. Isn't it true that in your statement for Mr. Blagojevic, you affirmatively state you never saw Mr. Blagojevic or Colonel Blagojevic anywhere around in the Bratunac area, correct? Or in the IKM, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Not correct. I did not see him, but during that period of time I did not have any contacts with Colonel Blagojevic because he was far away from my IKM and after the 11th I wasn't there. I wasn't there between the 11th and the 16th, so there was no way for me to see him at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What about prior to the 11th? Did you see him at all at the IKM, sir?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: He arrived either on the 6th or on some other date, I don't know exactly when, together with the signals soldier. He made rounds of some parts of our units. I don't know where he went, who he saw, but after that I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask you a little bit about Bratunac area and can you tell me where -- how far is Kravica is from Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: 12 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And your family used to live there, correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Before 1992, they did, and after 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And what happened in 1992 that your family had to move from Kravica?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Kravica is a small village, which was encircled by a Muslim population, for their own safety my wife and my children as well as other women and children left the area of Kravica. Only my father and my mother remained there until Christmas 1993. And after that, my mother moved to Bratunac and my father was killed on the -- that day in a Muslim attack against our village.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, I have, sir, with all due respect, that your father was killed on the 17th of March, 1993, correct, that the attack on Kravica by the Muslims was on the 7th of January 1993.

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: No. My father was killed on the 17th of January and his body was found on the 17th of March, when the village was liberated, i.e. when the Serb forces entered the village of Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry about that, accept my sympathies, and I apologise for having to ask you. I'm curious to know, though, the people in the Kravica village there, where did most of them go to? Where did they leave and live after the village was attacked and taken over by the Muslims in 1992?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Many people came to Bratunac and settled where they could in the free area. Some left for Serbia and never returned to the village afterwards. So that now half of the population of the village is gone.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Sir, did you ever discuss your upcoming testify with Dragoslav Trisic?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I have known Mr. Trisic since '87 because I worked for a company which -- in which the manager was his brother, so we've known each other for a long time. We may have touched upon this issue talking about something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you for sure. We see each other rather often because we are in the same line of business. His wife and I run some agency, so we meet over business too.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, do you know if he ever testified in any case here in the ICTY, the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know that he testified in -- do you know which case he testified in?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was the trial of Colonel Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And, sir, do you know if -- and I forgot to ask you this and I apologise, when you met with OTP's investigator, did they take notes when they talked to you?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: No. They only referred to my statement that I gave in the context of the Blagojevic trial, and they said that I might be become a Prosecution witness in some coming trial, but they didn't take any notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know if they recorded your statement, if they didn't, or do you recall?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know. I have a typed -- the typed statement given for the Blagojevic trial. That's about all I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, how long was your interview with Mr. Blaszczyk?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: With the investigator?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Half an hour, maybe -- it was more about private issues, where I lived, what I did. I think that we met in my office in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, in reviewing your statement before you testified today, with my learned friend Mr. Vanderpuye, did he also show you other transcripts or -- of other witnesses?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did he share with you what other witnesses said during your interview with him?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in the statement that you gave to Mr. -- or to Colonel Blagojevic in 2004, April 8th, that you don't have any of the dates that -- as so when you claim you saw Mr. Beara? Do you realise that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I know that statement, but they never asked me about any details,. So I gave just a general statements, but nobody asked me about any dates when I was giving my statement for the Blagojevic trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, how long was your meeting with the Blagojevic Defence team in preparation for your statement?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. It was one day. But I didn't really -- time didn't mean much to me so I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How did the Blagojevic team get to know you? How did they approach you? Did someone tell them, "You should go speak to Mr. Momcilovic"?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Many of us met Mr. Lugonic there, who was one of the investigators in the Blagojevic trial. It was -- we met him by chance, and when he was looking for witnesses for the Blagojevic trial, he was able -- he could find as many as he wanted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. How many times did you meet with them? Once only or more than once?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Once, I believe, and the second meeting was informal.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How do you remember, sir, I'm curious to know, 12 years after this sighting of Mr. Beara, that you saw him on a specific date, but you don't know anything that may have occurred in other parts of the town where you grew up and lived? Can you explain that to me?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know how, I don't know what happened, and I don't understand the second part of your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, the point of my question, sir, is how do you know as you sit here today that you purportedly saw Mr. Beara on July 11th, 1995, as opposed to in 1993 or 1996 or at no time? How do you remember that specific date, July 11th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I remember because he came with Mr. Deronjic and that was more or less the same day of my stay at the IKM. I saw them very briefly. I don't know where they went afterward, because that was the day when our job at the IKM was completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, when did you see Mr. Beara's image on TV?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, do you know if it was sometime in 1995 or 1996?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: It may have been in late 1995 or in 1996. I don't know for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm suggesting to you that that's impossible because there was no image that was broadcast whatsoever of Mr. Beara at that time up until the year 2000. Do you realise that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Could be. I told you I didn't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I suggest to you, sir, that you did not see Mr. Beara at the IKM on July 11th, 1995, and that it is absolutely not accurate, your testimony that you saw him for those few minutes that you claim you did. Would I be correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, you said that you didn't know Mr. Beara before and you never saw him after. Who told you that the person purportedly at the IKM was Mr. Beara?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: He arrived with the late Miroslav Deronjic and someone who was around knew that those people were the two of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, who? That's what I'm asking you. Who told you? Your memory seems to be accurate for dates. Now, tell me who told you that Mr. Beara was at the IKM.

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Someone present at Pribicevac. I couldn't give you the name now. There were many soldiers there. Somebody did know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How many times did Davidovic visit the IKM when you were there in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I remember only one occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How many times did Deronjic visit the IKM in 1995?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I saw him only once.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: This forward command post, sir, did they have to the best of your knowledge a logbook to write in who would be coming in and out of that IKM?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: They didn't?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: That was not an area that was rather which there was a fence. It was an open camp and around it there were woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, let me ask you this: You know Mr. Momir Nikolic. Do you know what his job was in Bratunac in July of 1995? Do you know what position he held?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: He was head of security for the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And you know, sir, because on page 20 today on lines 12 through 14 here is what you said, "I don't know about these things, and so even today I don't know what security officers do." So what I'm trying to figure out is if Momir Nikolic was a friend of yours, and if you came to testify on his behalf as a character witness, which we know you did on October 27th, 2003, how do you say that you don't know what security officers do? Did you ever discuss with Momir Nikolic what he does?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I was a quartermaster. And the office of the head of security was next door, but we -- I don't really know about these things. We never spoke about that, and he wasn't a man who would speak about these things. At least not to people for whom it didn't matter what he did. So if you were to ask me what security officers do, even now I couldn't answer. I was a quartermaster because I had a training in economy and that's what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I know you're a quartermaster, I'm not suggesting that you were anything else at that time, but I'm curious to know, here is a childhood friend, a school friend, a neighbour or his family -- is neighbours with your wife's family as you so testified in October of 2003. Did Momir Nikolic ever tell you what happened in Bratunac in July of 1995 with the Muslims from Srebrenica? Did he ever talk to you about that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: No. He really spoke very little about the -- about -- after those events. We more spoke about fishing and other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What about with Mr. Deronjic? Did you talk to him about the events as they unfolded in July of 1995 or as with Mr. Nikolic, you just talked about fishing?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I know Mr. Deronjic but we are not close friends. So we don't socialise. We may have had a drink occasionally. He had -- he socialised with other people. So I didn't have much contact with Colonel Deronjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, it says Colonel Deronjic. I don't know if you said Colonel. I think Mr. Deronjic, or if you think he's a Colonel, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. No, no. Not Colonel. Mr. Deronjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It was in the transcript. I didn't think you said it, but it was in the transcript so thank you for that. Sir, did you discuss with -- strike that. Did you ever join the SDS party?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know what party Mr. Davidovic is in?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: I think he's an SDS member.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Are you a member or were you a member of any party in 1995, political party?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: No. Only in 1996 I was a member of the SPS, the Communist Party, for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, I want to go back to this purported sighting of Mr. Beara at the IKM, and you stated that you don't know the purpose of the visit, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And you said that they came to see the view, the panoramic view, from the IKM, correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
utterances.text: That is my assessment of the purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What I'd like to know, sir, is how often or how far were -- was the place where you allegedly saw Mr. Beara from where the IKM is located. Is it one building, is it one office?

utterances.speaker: BOZO MOMCILOVIC
